apiIntro: Everything Marquee's Mac and Windows apps do goes through this JSON API, and dashboards, scripts and other tools can use it too. The machine-readable description is <link>/api/v1/openapi.json</link> (OpenAPI 3.1) — import it into Postman, Insomnia or any OpenAPI viewer.
apiSigningInBody: Every path below starts with /api/v1. Tools use an API key the admin creates under Settings › Integrations › API keys, sent as X-Api-Key: mq_… or Authorization: Bearer mq_… — never in the URL. A read-only key can call the endpoints marked “Any key”; a full key also those marked “Full key”. No key can reach the ones marked “No keys”. A key does what the account it acts as may do: the admin's, or a household member's.
apiErrorsBody: Errors are {shape} with the matching status: 401 for a missing, expired or revoked key, 403 outside its scope, 429 after too many wrong keys.
colorsIntro: Posters carry a thin colored strip along their bottom edge and a small badge in the corner that say where each title stands in your library. {note} Titles that aren't in your library get no strip at all.
badgesBody: The same colors appear on the badge on a poster, on a title's own page and next to search suggestions.
colorsRequestsNote: On the Requests page, “Can't find” and “Couldn't add” use the Missing red too: the request was approved, but the title isn't there yet. Look up an error message in the <link>error reference</link>.
errorsIntro: What every error message in Marquee actually means, and what to do about it. If the exact wording you saw isn't below, it's most likely a message passed straight through from Sonarr, Radarr, Plex, or Jellyfin themselves — check that service's own logs.
errSonarrNotConnectedMeaning: No Sonarr connection is saved, or it's missing a root folder / quality profile.
errSonarrNotConnectedWhatToDo: Go to Settings → Integrations and finish the Sonarr setup (URL, API key, then pick defaults).
errRadarrNotConnectedMeaning: Same as above, but for Radarr (movies).
errRadarrNotConnectedWhatToDo: Go to Settings → Integrations and finish the Radarr setup.
errSonarrNoTvdbMessage: Couldn't resolve this show for Sonarr.
errSonarrNoTvdbMeaning: Sonarr looks shows up by TVDB id, not TMDb id. TMDb's own record for this show has no linked TVDB id, so Marquee has nothing to hand Sonarr.
errSonarrNoTvdbWhatToDo: This is a data gap on TMDb, not a connection problem. On the Requests page, an "Add manually in Sonarr" link appears next to this error to jump straight to Sonarr's own search. Once you've found and downloaded it yourself, hit "Manually approve" (which replaces the Approve button here) so the requester sees it as handled instead of stuck pending.
errRadarrAddFailedMessage: Couldn't add this movie to Radarr.
errRadarrAddFailedMeaning: Radarr rejected the add request — wrong root folder, invalid quality profile, or Radarr itself returned an error.
errRadarrAddFailedWhatToDo: Check Radarr's own logs/UI, and confirm the root folder and quality profile saved in Settings still exist in Radarr.
errSonarrAddFailedMessage: Couldn't add this series to Sonarr.
errSonarrAddFailedMeaning: Sonarr rejected the add request after Marquee successfully resolved the TVDB id.
errSonarrAddFailedWhatToDo: Check Sonarr's own logs/UI, and confirm the root folder and quality profile saved in Settings still exist in Sonarr.
errNotInLibraryMessage: Couldn't find this title in your library.
errNotInLibraryMeaning: You tried to stop monitoring a title that isn't in the local sync cache (it may have already been removed).
errNotInLibraryWhatToDo: Refresh the page. If it persists, hit "Sync now" in Settings → Integrations.
errMonitoringFailedMeaning: Sonarr/Radarr didn't accept the monitoring change.
errMonitoringFailedWhatToDo: Try again; if it keeps failing, check that Sonarr/Radarr is reachable from Marquee.
errAdminOnlyAddMessage: Only the admin can add titles.
errAdminOnlyAddMeaning: Adding directly to Sonarr/Radarr is an admin-only action — members use Request instead.
errAdminOnlyAddWhatToDo: Use the Request button, or ask the admin to add it.
errAlreadyRequestedMeaning: You already have an active (pending or approved) request for this exact title.
errAlreadyRequestedWhatToDo: Check the Requests page for its current status instead of requesting again.
errAlreadyOwnedMessage: You already have this in your library.
errAlreadyOwnedMeaning: The title became owned or tracked between when you loaded the page and when you hit Request.
errAlreadyOwnedWhatToDo: Refresh the page — it should now show as already in your library.
errRequestNotFoundMessage: Request not found or already reviewed.
errRequestNotFoundMeaning: Someone (possibly you, in another tab) already approved or rejected this request.
errRequestNotFoundWhatToDo: Refresh the Requests page to see its current state.
errRequestAlreadyReviewedMeaning: A second approve/reject landed after the first one already went through — a race, not a bug.
errRequestAlreadyReviewedWhatToDo: Refresh the page; no action needed.
errUrlKeyRequiredMessage: URL and API key are required.
errUrlKeyRequiredMeaning: The connect form was submitted with one of the two fields empty.
errUrlKeyRequiredWhatToDo: Fill in both the server URL and API key.
errConnectFailedMessage: Couldn't connect. Check the URL and API key and try again.
errConnectFailedMeaning: Marquee reached out to the server (Sonarr, Radarr, or Jellyfin) and it didn't respond as expected — wrong URL, wrong/expired API key, or the server is down.
errConnectFailedWhatToDo: Double-check the URL is reachable from wherever Marquee is running (not just your own browser), and that the API key is current.
errTmdbTokenInvalidMessage: Couldn't verify this token with TMDb. Check it and try again.
errTmdbTokenInvalidMeaning: The TMDb access token you entered was rejected by TMDb's API.
errTmdbTokenInvalidWhatToDo: Generate a fresh API Read Access Token from your TMDb account settings and paste the whole thing.
errTmdbTokenMissingMeaning: The TMDb token field was submitted empty.
errTmdbTokenMissingWhatToDo: Paste your TMDb API Read Access Token.
errSyncFailedMessage: Some integrations failed to sync — check their connection.
errSyncFailedMeaning: "Sync now" ran, and at least one connected integration (Plex, Jellyfin, Sonarr, or Radarr) failed partway through.
errSyncFailedWhatToDo: The others still synced fine. Check each integration's card in Settings for a stale "last synced" time to spot which one is failing.
errPlexStartFailedMessage: Couldn't start Plex sign-in. Try again.
errPlexStartFailedMeaning: Marquee couldn't get a sign-in PIN from Plex's own servers — usually a transient network issue.
errPlexStartFailedWhatToDo: Try connecting Plex again in a moment.
errBadCredentialsMeaning: Exactly what it says — the credentials didn't match.
errBadCredentialsWhatToDo: Double-check for typos, or ask the admin to reset your password from Settings.
errTooManyAttemptsMessage: Too many attempts. Try again in a few minutes.
errTooManyAttemptsMeaning: Repeated failed sign-in attempts triggered a short rate limit, to slow down password guessing.
errTooManyAttemptsWhatToDo: Wait a few minutes before trying again.
errUsernameTakenMessage: An account with that username already exists
errUsernameTakenMeaning: Someone (possibly you already) has that exact username.
errEditOwnOnlyMessage: You can only edit your own account.
errEditOwnOnlyMeaning: Non-admin accounts can't edit anyone else's profile.
errEditOwnOnlyWhatToDo: Ask the admin to make the change from Settings → Household members.
errPlexNoAccessMessage: This Plex account doesn't have access to this server.
errPlexNoAccessMeaning: You signed in to Plex with an account the admin's Plex server isn't shared with, so it can't be used here.
errPlexNoAccessWhatToDo: Sign in to Plex with the account the admin shares their server with, or ask them to share it with you.
errPlexNoAccountMessage: There's no Marquee account for this Plex account yet. Ask the admin to add you.
errPlexNoAccountMeaning: Plex/Jellyfin checked out, but there's no Marquee account for you yet and the admin has turned off new accounts from Plex/Jellyfin sign-in.
errPlexNoAccountWhatToDo: Ask the admin to import you (Settings → Account → Import from your media server) or turn new accounts back on.
errJellyfinBadCredentialsMeaning: The household's Jellyfin server didn't accept those credentials (or that Jellyfin user is disabled).
errJellyfinBadCredentialsWhatToDo: Use the username and password you use for Jellyfin itself.
errPlexExpiredMessage: That Plex sign-in expired. Try again.
errPlexExpiredMeaning: Plex sign-in waits 10 minutes for you to approve it on plex.tv, and each one can only be used once.
errPlexExpiredWhatToDo: Start again with Sign in with Plex and finish in the tab that opens.
errPlexLinkedElsewhereMessage: This Plex account is already linked to another Marquee account.
errPlexLinkedElsewhereMeaning: Each Plex (or Jellyfin) account can sign in to only one Marquee account.
errPlexLinkedElsewhereWhatToDo: Unlink it from the other account first, or ask the admin.
errSsoNotAllowedMessage: Your Authentik account isn't allowed to use Marquee. Ask the admin to add you to the right group.
errSsoNotAllowedMeaning: Single sign-on worked, but the admin only lets people in a certain group (in Authentik, Authelia, or whichever sign-in the household uses) into Marquee, and you're not in it.
errSsoNotAllowedWhatToDo: Ask the admin to add you to that group in the identity provider, then sign in again.
errSsoNoAccountMessage: There's no Marquee account for this Authentik account yet. Ask the admin to add you.
errSsoNoAccountMeaning: Single sign-on worked, but no Marquee account is linked to that identity and the admin has new accounts from single sign-on turned off.
errSsoNoAccountWhatToDo: Sign in with your Marquee password and link it under Settings → Account → Linked accounts, or ask the admin to turn new accounts on.
errSsoExpiredMessage: That Authentik sign-in expired or was already used. Try again.
errSsoExpiredMeaning: Single sign-on has to finish within 10 minutes, in the same browser it started in, and each attempt works once.
errSsoExpiredWhatToDo: Start again with the Sign in with … button.
errQuickConnectOffMessage: Quick Connect is turned off on this Jellyfin server. The admin can turn it on in Jellyfin's Dashboard → General.
errQuickConnectOffMeaning: Quick Connect lets you sign in by approving a code in a Jellyfin app, but the Jellyfin server has it switched off.
errQuickConnectOffWhatToDo: Sign in with your Jellyfin username and password instead, or ask the admin to turn Quick Connect on.
errQuickConnectExpiredMessage: That Quick Connect code expired. Try again.
errQuickConnectExpiredMeaning: A Quick Connect code works for a few minutes and only once.
errQuickConnectExpiredWhatToDo: Choose Use Quick Connect again and enter the new code in your Jellyfin app.
errSignInRequiredMeaning: The action needs a signed-in session, and none was found (it may have expired).
errNoFilterMatchesMessage: Nothing matches those filters — try loosening them.
errNoFilterMatchesMeaning: The Discover page's random-pick or filtered search came back empty for the current filter combination.
errNoFilterMatchesWhatToDo: Remove a filter (genre, year range, etc.) and try again.
